# Schema

A theme is a plain TypeScript object that defines the colors used by the components in this library. Components read their colors from the active theme instead of hard-coding them, so you can restyle everything by changing one object.

Three themes are built in: `default`, `ocean` and `forest`. You can also pass your own schema, with no changes to the library.


## Default theme

The full schema of the `default` theme, generated from the source code so it is always up to date.

<Source language="json" code={JSON.stringify(THEMES.default, null, 2)} />

## Using a built-in theme

Wrap your app (or any part of it) in `Theme` and choose a theme with `name`. If you omit it, `default` is used.

```tsx
<Theme name="ocean">
  <App />
</Theme>
```

## Using your own schema

Pass a schema object to the `schema` prop. It follows the structure above and takes priority over `name`.

```tsx
import { Theme, ThemeSchema } from 'najwer23morsels/lib/Theme';

const sunset: ThemeSchema = {
  name: 'Sunset',
  components: {
    button: {
      variants: {
        primary: {
          background: '#C2410C',
          border: '#9A3412',
          text: '#FFFFFF',
          focus: '#C2410C',
        },
        // ...all other variants
      },
    },
    typography: {
      colors: {
        body: { color: '#292524' },
        // ...all other tokens
      },
    },
  },
};

<Theme schema={sunset}>
  <App />
</Theme>
```

Typing the object as `ThemeSchema` makes TypeScript report missing or misspelled keys.

### Tips

- **Define every variant and token.** The schema is a full `schema`, not a partial one.
- **Keep text readable.** Check that `text` has enough contrast against `background` (WCAG AA recommends 4.5:1 for normal text).
- **Scope a theme to part of the page.** Colors are applied to the wrapping element, so you can nest `Theme` components to style one section differently.
- **Target a theme in CSS.** The wrapper sets a `data-n23m-theme` attribute with the theme `name`, and adds the `n23mTheme` class.
